pois.name: Dense coral mound cluster
pois.note: Real survey terrain: this tile shows ~72 m of local relief around this point (744.2 m at the sample coordinate against a shallower rim nearby), inside the tile's bbox (part of the wider Blake Plateau coral province mapped by Sowers et al. 2024). At this tile's ~53 x 61 m cell size, individual coral colonies and small mounds are not resolved, but the broader mound-field relief is real terrain, not invented.

pois.name: Desmophyllum pertusum thicket
pois.note: The mound terrain here is real (this tile), but the coral colonies themselves are placed reconstructions -- this game's terrain resolution cannot show individual coral heads. Desmophyllum pertusum is documented as the dominant reef-building species across the wider Blake Plateau province (Sowers et al. 2024, NOAA); its presence at this exact point is inferred from that province-wide finding, not a site-specific survey record, hence medium rather than high confidence.

pois.name: A neighbouring mound
pois.note: The GMRT grid reads 775.5 m at this marker, about 294 m southwest of the core scan. These local depths do not establish the position of an individual coral mound in the Sowers et al. 2024 classification. The scan samples regional terrain; no colony coordinate is claimed.

pois.name: Channel between mounds
pois.note: The GMRT grid reads 779.7 m at this point, lower than the core marker at 744.2 m. The terrain depth alone does not establish a surveyed channel between individual coral mounds.
